requirements.condition: A token is presented for redemption at current_time >= expires_at.
requirements.behavior: Reject redemption without changing membership; expiry equality is invalid.
acceptance: For an otherwise legitimate unused token at current_time == expires_at, redemption is rejected and membership before and after is identical.
Repeat with current_time > expires_at; redemption is rejected and membership is unchanged.
The expiry predicate is current_time < expires_at; an otherwise legitimate unused token strictly before expiry remains eligible under REQ-INV-005.
unchanged_behavior: Legitimate unused, unexpired tokens remain usable.

requirements.condition: A token has already produced one successful redemption.
requirements.behavior: It never produces another successful redemption, regardless of current membership or the principal presenting it.
acceptance: After one successful redemption, a later attempt with the same token and principal cannot succeed again.
After that successful redemption and removal of its membership, a later attempt with the same still-unexpired token cannot succeed or recreate membership.
After one successful redemption, presenting that still-unexpired token for a different principal cannot succeed or grant that principal membership.
unchanged_behavior: Use of a different legitimate unused, unexpired token is not prohibited by consumption of this token.

requirements.condition: Two simultaneous attempts present the same legitimate unused, unexpired token.
requirements.behavior: No more than one attempt succeeds; concurrency must preserve the token lifetime limit in REQ-INV-002.
acceptance: For two simultaneous attempts with the same token and same principal, the combined count of successful redemptions is at most one.
For two simultaneous attempts with the same token and two distinct eligible principals, the combined count of successful redemptions is at most one; both must not gain membership through that token.
Any subsequent attempt remains subject to REQ-INV-002 if either simultaneous attempt succeeded.
unchanged_behavior: The normal legitimate unused-token case in REQ-INV-005 remains supported; rejecting every request is not a compliant resolution.

acceptance: For a token known to be invalid, compare membership before and after the attempted redemption: no membership changes and no success.
Expiry-invalid cases include equality and later times under REQ-INV-001; other invalid-token classifications require the clarification recorded in ASM-INV-004.
unchanged_behavior: Valid unused tokens retain the successful path in REQ-INV-005.

requirements.condition: An eligible recipient without team membership submits a legitimate unused token while current_time < expires_at, with no competing attempt.
requirements.behavior: The token works: redemption succeeds and grants the recipient membership in the invited team.
acceptance: Given a legitimate unused token, an eligible recipient without that team membership, and current_time strictly before expires_at, a normal uncontended redemption succeeds and creates the intended membership.
After this success, the token is subject to REQ-INV-002.
Existing-member handling is unresolved under ASM-INV-003; this positive case does not decide that behavior.
unchanged_behavior: The team-owner invitation and recipient redemption purpose remains intact.

non_goals: Selecting a persistence mechanism, transaction boundary, locking or other concurrency architecture.
Implementation, executable task planning, test execution, external publication, installation or acceptance of unresolved choices.
Changing token issuance, membership removal, eligibility or unrelated membership behavior beyond the stated redemption guarantees.

assumptions.text: DES-INV-001 assumes current membership for the presenting principal can stand in for the token lifetime redemption history. Policy contradicts that sufficiency after membership removal or a principal change. The technical replacement remains open; hold dependent design/task approval for REQ-INV-002.

DES-INV-001 leaves concurrency coordination unspecified and supplies only uniqueness of (team_id, principal_id). That constraint does not establish one winner per token across distinct principals. A token-wide concurrency guarantee and its failure boundary need architecture review; hold dependent design/task approval for REQ-INV-002 and REQ-INV-003.

DES-INV-001 returns already_redeemed when the principal already belongs to the team, even if the token has never been used. Whether such a request consumes the token, succeeds, or returns a distinct non-success outcome is unspecified by policy. Product decision required; hold this existing-member extension of REQ-INV-005 and its REQ-INV-002 implications.

Policy fixes the strict expiry boundary but does not identify the authoritative clock/evaluation instant, legitimate-principal rules, the full set of invalid-token conditions, or API error mapping. Clarification is needed for those details in REQ-INV-001, REQ-INV-004 and REQ-INV-005. No numerical latency, clock tolerance or response-code target is proposed.
